reasoning: The plant displays classic green wilt — leaves drooping/hanging while still green with no spots, interveinal chlorosis, or lesions. This pattern is characteristic of Phytophthora root and stem rot in early-to-mid stage, where stem girdling at/below the soil line cuts off water supply before leaves brown. All other wilt-causing diseases (SDS, Brown Stem Rot) typically show interveinal chlorosis, and root/stem rots (Fusarium, Charcoal Rot) show more advanced browning.
